question: The manual says only which riders should carry passengers or large loads?
choice_a: Any licensed rider, regardless of experience
choice_b: Only riders on permits, to build skill
choice_c: Riders with a passenger endorsement course completed within the last year
explanation: Only experienced riders should carry passengers or large loads. The extra weight changes the way the motorcycle handles, balances, turns, speeds up, and slows down.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.31, 'Carrying Passengers and Cargo'

question: Before taking a passenger or heavy load on the street for the first time, the manual recommends you:
choice_b: Skip practice if you are an experienced rider
explanation: Before taking a passenger or heavy load on the street, practice away from traffic.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.31, 'Carrying Passengers and Cargo'

question: According to the manual, Pennsylvania law requires that any motorcycle carrying a passenger (other than in a sidecar or enclosed cab) be equipped with:
choice_a: Footrests and handholds for the passenger
explanation: PA law requires that any motorcycle carrying a passenger, other than in a side car or enclosed cab, must be equipped with footrests and handholds for the passenger.

question: When a passenger sits on the seat with you before a ride, the manual says you should adjust:
choice_a: Only the rear brake pedal height
choice_b: The mirrors and headlight, according to the change in the motorcycle's angle
choice_c: Nothing, since passenger weight doesn't change the motorcycle's angle
explanation: While your passenger sits on the seat with you, adjust the mirrors and headlight according to the change in the motorcycle's angle.

question: The manual instructs a passenger to get on the motorcycle only:
choice_b: After the motorcycle is already moving
choice_d: After you have started the engine
explanation: Tell your passenger to get on the motorcycle only after you have started the engine.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.31-32, 'Instructing Passengers'

question: The manual tells passengers to keep both feet on the footpegs:
choice_a: Only while the motorcycle is moving
choice_c: Even when the motorcycle is stopped
choice_d: Only when instructed by the rider at each stop
explanation: Tell your passenger to keep both feet on the pegs, even when stopped.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.32, 'Instructing Passengers'

question: The manual instructs a passenger to lean:
choice_a: As the rider leans, staying directly behind the rider
choice_b: Opposite the rider's lean to help balance
choice_c: Only during straight-line riding, never in turns
choice_d: Independently of the rider, based on their own sense of balance
explanation: Tell your passenger to stay directly behind you, leaning as you lean.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.32, 'Instructing Passengers'

question: The manual says you should tell your passenger to tighten their hold in all of the following situations EXCEPT:
choice_b: When cruising at a steady speed on an open, empty highway
choice_c: When you are about to start from a stop
choice_d: When you will make a sudden move
explanation: Tell your passenger to tighten their hold when you approach surface problems, are about to start from a stop, or warn that you will make a sudden move -- not simply while cruising steadily.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.32, 'Instructing Passengers'

question: With a passenger aboard, the manual says the motorcycle will respond:
choice_a: Exactly the same as riding solo
choice_b: Faster, because of the added momentum
choice_c: More slowly only when braking, but not when accelerating
choice_d: More slowly, especially the heavier the passenger
explanation: Your motorcycle will respond more slowly with a passenger on board. The heavier your passenger, the longer it may take to slow down, speed up, or turn -- especially on a light motorcycle.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.32, 'Riding With Passengers'

question: When riding with a passenger, the manual recommends you:
choice_a: Brake later than usual to compensate for the added weight
choice_b: Follow more closely to keep the group compact
choice_c: Start slowing earlier as you approach a stop and open up a larger cushion of space
choice_d: Take curves and bumps at your normal solo speed
explanation: Start slowing earlier as you approach a stop, and open up a larger cushion of space ahead and to the sides; ride a little slower, especially when taking curves, corners, or bumps.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.32, 'Riding With Passengers'

question: To avoid raising the motorcycle's center of gravity and disturbing its balance, the manual warns against:
choice_a: Piling loads against a sissybar or frame on the back of the seat
choice_c: Keeping loads low and fastened securely
choice_d: Using a tank bag for light items
explanation: Keep the Load Low -- fasten loads securely or put them in saddle bags. Piling loads against a sissybar or frame on the back of the seat raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and disturbs its balance.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.32, 'Carrying Loads'

question: The manual warns that mounting loads behind the rear axle can:
choice_b: Affect how the motorcycle turns and brakes, and can cause a wobble
choice_d: Only matter at highway speeds above 55 mph
explanation: Mounting loads behind the rear axle can affect how the motorcycle turns and brakes. It can also cause a wobble.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.32, 'Carrying Loads'

question: The manual recommends securing a load with elastic cords rather than rope because:
choice_a: Rope is illegal to use for securing cargo in Pennsylvania
choice_b: Elastic cords are always cheaper than rope
choice_c: Rope adds too much weight to the load
choice_d: Rope tends to stretch and knots come loose, letting the load shift or fall
explanation: Fasten the load securely with elastic cords (bungee cords or nets); rope tends to stretch and knots come loose, permitting the load to shift or fall.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.32, 'Carrying Loads'

question: The manual advises stopping periodically during a ride to:
choice_a: Reload the saddlebags with new items
choice_c: Check that the load has not worked loose or moved
choice_d: Check tire tread depth with a gauge
explanation: Check the Load -- stop and check the load every so often to make sure it has not worked loose or moved.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.33, 'Carrying Loads'
